To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• The hosting capacity for a feeder decreases as the feeder load increases.

(i) the PV hosting capacity for a feeder is highly correlated to the feeder’s load and the percent of issues caused by the PV; (ii) the PV hosting capacities for different feeder volt-ages are not significantly different; and (iii) the locational PV host-ing capacity at each bus is highly dependent on the bus’s load and the PV’s distance from the bus.
• The feeder hosting capacity and locational PV capacity are highly dependent on the feeder load.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How much PV can each feeder handle?

how to determine the PV hosting capacity for each feeder, the locational PV host capacity for every bus on the feeder, and how to use this information to better understand the impact of PV penetration on the power distribution system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PV hosting capacity is a function of the load, the percent of issues caused by the PV, and the voltage.
the feeder load is a poor indicator of the hosting capacity.
the hosting capacity of the distribution feeder depends on the feeder load, the feeder voltage, and the location of the PV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
feeder loading is not a good indicator of feeder hosting capacity, and the variation in hosting capacity is much larger for low voltage feeder systems.
feeder load and voltage are not good indicators of the feeder PV hosting capacity.
there is a strong correlation between PV hosting capacity and feeder load, and a weak correlation between PV hosting and feeder voltage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the feeder hosting capacity can be correlated with the feeder load.
the hosting capacity of a distribution feeder is highly correlated with the feeder load, and that the hosting capacity is not significantly different for different feeder voltaged.
the hosting capacity is a function of the feeder loading and that the PV hosting capacity can be predicted based on the feeder loading.
